title.narrative: ED emergency support to Sri Lanka post cyclone Ditwah

description.narrative:
Cyclone Ditwah struck Sri Lanka from 27–29 November, causing the worst flooding and landslides in over two decades. All 25 districts were affected, 22 declared disaster zones, impacting 2.2 million people (612,000 families). As of mid-December 2025, 639 deaths and 193 missing were reported, with over 233,000 people sheltered in nearly 1,000 centres at peak displacement.
The cyclone caused severe damage to housing, infrastructure, and essential services: 5,300 houses destroyed, 85,000 damaged; major transport disruption; power outages for 3.9 million; and water supply loss for 2.5 million, heightening health risks.
Preliminary assessments indicate 1,185 schools and 2,720 preschools in flood-affected areas, with 10–23% damaged, while many remain in use as safety shelters. The disaster coincided with national examinations, leading to the indefinite postponement of the GCE Advanced Level (A/L) exams, increasing stress among learners. All early childhood development centres have remained closed since 28 November 2025, affecting 68,000 preschool-age children.
Overall, an estimated 458,609 school-age children, 28,900 teachers and school leaders, and nearly 900 children with disabilities have been affected. Over 60% of children lost essential learning materials, and prolonged school closures and overcrowded shelters have heightened protection and mental health risks, especially children and adolescent girls.
On 29 November 2025, the President of Sri Lanka declared a State of Emergency and requested international assistance. Furthermore, on 19 December 2025, the Secretary-General of the Sri Lanka National Commission for UNESCO sent detailed requests to DIR/UNESCO New Delhi for UNESCO's immediate support to restore minimum standards for safe and child-friendly learning environments.
This Special Account Project will be UNESCO's response to the Sri Lanka Ditwah cyclone emergency and provide: (a) support for the continuity of learning in Colombo and Kegalle Districts; (b) immediate Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) through education systems.
